A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cortical injury in MS is driven by a combination of immune mediated and degenera-tive mechanisms, which are likely to involve the release of diffusible toxins from the meninges by peripheral immune cells, as well as the direct interaction between peripheral immune and meningeal resident cells, which is mediated in part by the expression of specific cell surface receptors on the peripheral immune cells.

the meningeal compartment in progressive MS is the site for chronic immune cell infiltration and activation, which leads to the production and release of inflammatory mediators that drive subpial demyelination and cortical injury.
we have shown that the meninges and Virchow Robin Spaces (VRS) in the MS brain contain immune cells that produce inflammatory mediators that can cause cortical damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cortical injury in progressive MS may be driven in part by immune cell mediated injury within the meninges, and that the meningeal niche may be an important target for future therapeutic development.

cortical injury in progressive MS is driven by a combination of inflammatory processes, and that a better understanding of the role of the CNS compartment in disease pathology will help to identify more specific and efficacious therapeutic strategies.
cortical injury in MS is not a passive process but rather is actively driven by a dynamic interaction between immune and CNS resident cell populations.
